cards.hypothesis: Subject-specific autonomic reactivity patterns cause non-exchangeability within Mondrian taxonomy bins, violating the conditional coverage guarantee for high-reactivity individuals
cards.proposed_mechanism: High autonomic reactivity subjects exhibit EDA and HRV response magnitudes that fall outside the calibration distribution of their assigned Mondrian bin, causing prediction sets to be systematically too narrow for their actual stress responses
cards.causal_path: Subject trait (high autonomic reactivity) → Extreme physiological response magnitude during stress → Response falls outside calibration bin's empirical quantile range → Conformal prediction set too narrow → Undercoverage
control_variables: include baseline_eda as covariate in bin assignment
match on age/sex in calibration set
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage stems from sensor noise artifacts during high-movement stress periods, not autonomic reactivity per se
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage correlates with ACC magnitude during stress, not with autonomic reactivity scores measured during rest
cards.distinguishing_test: Regress per-subject coverage gap against both autonomic reactivity score and mean ACC during stress; reactivity should remain significant predictor after controlling for ACC
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior WESAD analyses show ~30% of subjects have EDA responses >2 SD from mean; Mondrian bins typically contain 10-20 subjects, so extreme responders likely fall outside bin quantiles
minimum_data_needed: per-subject EDA/HRV time series during stress/rest
Mondrian bin assignments for each calibration point
per-subject coverage indicators at nominal 90% level
ACC data for movement artifact quantification
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in top tertile of autonomic reactivity score will show coverage <80% at nominal 90% level, while bottom tertile will show coverage ≥88%
cards.failure_condition: No significant correlation between autonomic reactivity score and per-subject coverage gap (p>0.05) after controlling for movement
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage_gap ~ reactivity_tertile + mean_stress_ACC + (1|subject), test reactivity_tertile coefficient
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian bins using reactivity-stratified taxonomy; if undercoverage persists for high-reactivity subjects, the mechanism is falsified

cards.hypothesis: Wrist-worn sensor signal quality degradation during stress-induced vasoconstriction causes systematic underestimation of EDA amplitude in calibration, leading to narrow prediction sets
cards.proposed_mechanism: Stress-induced peripheral vasoconstriction reduces wrist skin conductance signal-to-noise ratio, causing the EDA feature extractor to underestimate true sympathetic activation during calibration; test-time stress responses then exceed predicted ranges
cards.causal_path: Stress → Peripheral vasoconstriction → Reduced wrist EDA signal amplitude + increased noise → Feature extractor underestimates phasic EDA peaks → Calibration nonconformity scores too small → Prediction sets too narrow → Undercoverage
control_variables: use chest EDA as ground truth for sympathetic activation
cards.rival_explanation: Chest and wrist EDA measure different physiological phenomena; discrepancy reflects true physiological difference not sensor artifact
cards.rival_prediction: Wrist-chest EDA discrepancy correlates with vasoconstriction proxy (finger temperature drop) but coverage gap does not
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute wrist-chest EDA ratio during stress; if mechanism holds, ratio should predict coverage gap. If rival holds, ratio predicts physiological difference but not coverage gap
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD wrist EDA known to have 40-60% lower amplitude than chest during stress; vasoconstriction can reduce wrist signal by additional 30-50% based on vascular physiology literature
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with largest wrist-chest EDA amplitude ratio drop during stress will show greatest undercoverage; wrist EDA tonic level during stress negatively correlates with coverage
cards.failure_condition: Wrist-chest EDA ratio during stress does not correlate with per-subject coverage gap (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Spearman correlation between (chest_eda_peak - wrist_eda_peak)/chest_eda_peak during stress and per-subject coverage gap; permutation test n=10000
cards.falsification_test: Replace wrist EDA features with chest EDA features in Mondrian predictor; if undercoverage disappears for previously affected subjects, mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified

cards.hypothesis: Non-stationary physiological baselines across the WESAD protocol timeline cause calibration-test distribution shift within Mondrian bins
cards.proposed_mechanism: The WESAD protocol induces progressive physiological adaptation (habituation/sensitization) across conditions; calibration data from early conditions don't represent test condition distributions for subjects with strong temporal trends
cards.causal_path: Protocol progression (baseline → amusement → stress → meditation → recovery) → Progressive physiological adaptation (e.g., EDA habituation, HRV sensitization) → Calibration conditions (early) distribution ≠ Test condition (late) distribution within same Mondrian bin → Nonconformity scores miscalibrated → Undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to inherent subject heterogeneity, not temporal non-stationarity
cards.rival_prediction: Shuffling condition order labels destroys any temporal trend but coverage gap remains associated with subject ID
cards.distinguishing_test: Fit per-subject linear trend of EDA tonic across conditions; correlate trend slope with coverage gap. Under mechanism, significant correlation; under rival, no correlation after controlling for subject ID
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD protocol spans ~60 minutes; EDA habituation literature shows 10-30% tonic decline over similar durations; Mondrian bins pool across conditions, so shift could be substantial
minimum_data_needed: Mondrian bin assignments per calibration point
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with steepest negative EDA tonic trend across conditions will show largest undercoverage on late conditions (meditation/recovery)
cards.failure_condition: Per-subject EDA tonic trend slope does not predict coverage gap on late conditions (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Per-subject linear regression: EDA_tonic ~ condition_order; extract slope. Then: coverage_gap_late_conditions ~ slope + (1|subject_bin)
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian with condition-stratified taxonomy (separate bins per condition); if undercoverage disappears, mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified

cards.hypothesis: Stress label misalignment between self-report and physiological ground truth creates label noise that disproportionately affects Mondrian bins with ambiguous stress responses
cards.proposed_mechanism: Some subjects show physiological stress responses during 'non-stress' conditions (anticipatory anxiety) or fail to respond during 'stress' conditions (blunted responders); Mondrian bins pool these mislabeled points, corrupting nonconformity score distributions
cards.causal_path: Subject trait (anxiety/blunted response) → Physiological response mismatches labeled condition → Miscalibrated nonconformity scores in affected Mondrian bins → Prediction sets too narrow for true stress state → Undercoverage for affected subjects
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage reflects true physiological variability, not label noise
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage gap correlates with physiological variability within condition, not with label disagreement
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute per-subject label_agreement (correlation between self-report and physiological stress score across conditions); regress coverage gap on label_agreement controlling for within-condition physiological variance
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD self-report labels are coarse (binary stress/non-stress); literature suggests 15-25% label-physiology mismatch in stress studies; Mondrian bins with <80% purity could have substantially corrupted quantiles
minimum_data_needed: chest EDA and HRV per condition
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with low label_agreement (physiological response contradicts self-report) will show undercoverage specifically in bins with low label_purity
cards.failure_condition: Label agreement does not predict coverage gap after controlling for within-condition physiological variance (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: For each bin, compute label_purity = proportion of points where physiological_stress_score matches self_report. Mixed model: coverage_gap ~ label_purity + within_bin_physiological_variance + (1|subject)
cards.falsification_test: Re-label calibration data using physiological_stress_score threshold instead of self-report; if undercoverage resolves for mismatched subjects, mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian taxonomy based on discrete condition labels fails to capture continuous stress intensity gradients, causing undercoverage for subjects with intermediate stress responses
cards.proposed_mechanism: WESAD conditions represent ordinal stress levels (baseline < amusement < stress > meditation > recovery) but Mondrian treats them as nominal categories; subjects with intermediate responses fall between bins, receiving prediction sets calibrated for wrong intensity
cards.causal_path: Ordinal stress intensity continuum → Discrete Mondrian taxonomy (nominal bins) → Subjects with intermediate responses assigned to adjacent bins → Calibration quantiles from wrong intensity level → Prediction sets mismatched to true stress intensity → Undercoverage
control_variables: use ordinal taxonomy with intensity-ordered bins
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to within-bin heterogeneity unrelated to stress intensity ordering
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage gap correlates with within-bin feature variance, not with distance to bin intensity centroid
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute subject_intensity_bin_mismatch = |continuous_stress_intensity - bin_intensity_centroid|; test if mismatch predicts coverage gap better than within-bin variance
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD has 5 conditions; if stress intensity is roughly linear baseline→stress, intermediate conditions (amusement, meditation) may have 20-30% of subjects mismatched; effect depends on bin granularity
minimum_data_needed: continuous stress intensity measure per subject per condition (e.g., EDA+HRV composite)
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects whose continuous stress intensity falls between bin centroids will show lower coverage than those near centroids
cards.failure_condition: Intensity-bin mismatch does not predict coverage gap (p>0.05) after controlling for within-bin variance
cards.statistical_test_plan: Quantile regression: coverage_gap ~ intensity_bin_mismatch + within_bin_variance, test mismatch coefficient at τ=0.9
cards.falsification_test: Replace nominal Mondrian taxonomy with ordinal taxonomy (bins respect intensity ordering); if undercoverage for intermediate responders disappears, mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified

cards.hypothesis: Chest-worn sensor displacement during stress-induced movement creates heteroscedastic noise that violates Mondrian's exchangeability assumption within bins
cards.proposed_mechanism: Stress conditions involve more upper-body movement (typing, gesturing) causing chest sensor displacement; this increases ECG/RESP noise heteroscedastically for high-movement subjects, widening true conditional distribution beyond calibration quantiles
cards.causal_path: Stress condition → Increased upper-body movement → Chest sensor displacement → Heteroscedastic noise in ECG/RESP features → True conditional variance > calibration variance within bin → Prediction sets too narrow → Undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to genuine physiological variability increase during stress, not sensor noise
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage gap correlates with physiological variability markers (e.g., HRV complexity) not with signal quality indices
cards.distinguishing_test: Regress coverage gap on both chest_acc_magnitude and HRV_sample_entropy during stress; mechanism predicts ACC significant, entropy not; rival predicts opposite
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD chest ACC shows 2-3x increase during stress vs baseline; sensor displacement can increase ECG noise 5-10x; Mondrian bins pool across movement levels, so high-movement subjects' true variance underestimated
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with high chest ACC during stress will show undercoverage; coverage gap correlates with ACC magnitude but not with HRV complexity
cards.failure_condition: Chest ACC magnitude during stress does not predict coverage gap after controlling for HRV complexity (p>0.05)
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate using only low-movement periods (chest_acc < threshold); if undercoverage persists for high-movement subjects, mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Finite calibration set size per Mondrian bin causes quantile estimation error that disproportionately affects small bins containing rare physiological phenotypes
cards.proposed_mechanism: Mondrian bins with few calibration points (rare phenotypes: e.g., blunted responders, hyper-responders) have high quantile estimation variance; the 90th percentile nonconformity score is underestimated, yielding prediction sets that are too narrow
cards.causal_path: Rare physiological phenotype → Small Mondrian bin size (n_calibration) → High variance in empirical 90th percentile nonconformity score → Systematic underestimation of true 90th percentile (order statistic bias) → Prediction sets too narrow → Undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage for rare phenotypes reflects genuine distributional differences, not estimation error
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage gap persists even with infinite calibration data (simulated via bootstrap)
cards.distinguishing_test: Bootstrap calibration sets within each bin to estimate quantile estimation variance; correlate bin_size with bootstrap variance of 90th percentile; test if coverage gap correlates with bootstrap variance
cards.effect_size_rationale: Order statistic theory: for n=10, 90th percentile has ~30% relative standard error; WESAD has ~15 subjects, 5 conditions, Mondrian may create bins with n<5 for rare phenotypes
minimum_data_needed: Mondrian bin assignments for all calibration points
cards.testable_prediction: Bins with size <10 will show coverage <85% at nominal 90%; coverage gap negatively correlates with bin size
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between bin size and coverage gap (p>0.05); or bootstrap variance does not explain coverage gap
cards.statistical_test_plan: Bin-level regression: mean_coverage_gap ~ log(bin_size) + bin_feature_variance; subject-level: coverage_gap ~ bin_size + (1|bin)
cards.falsification_test: Augment calibration with synthetic data from fitted parametric distribution per bin; if undercoverage persists, mechanism falsified (not estimation error)

cards.hypothesis: Physiological recovery dynamics during the post-stress meditation condition create a non-exchangeable subpopulation within the 'recovery' Mondrian bin
cards.proposed_mechanism: Subjects differ in physiological recovery speed after stress; slow recoverers in the meditation condition have elevated sympathetic tone that resembles stress, but are binned with fast recoverers; calibration quantiles from mixed recovery states are too narrow for slow recoverers
cards.causal_path: Subject trait (slow physiological recovery) → Elevated EDA/HRV during meditation condition → Assigned to same Mondrian bin as fast recoverers → Calibration nonconformity scores reflect mixed recovery states → Prediction sets too narrow for slow recoverers → Undercoverage during meditation
cards.rival_explanation: Meditation condition undercoverage is due to meditation-specific physiological patterns (e.g., respiratory sinus arrhythmia) not recovery speed
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage gap during meditation correlates with respiration rate variability, not with EDA/HRV recovery time constants from stress
cards.distinguishing_test: Fit per-subject EDA exponential decay during recovery; correlate time constant with meditation coverage gap controlling for respiration variability
cards.effect_size_rationale: Recovery time constants vary 3-5x across individuals; WESAD meditation is 5-10 min post-stress; slow recoverers (τ>5min) still elevated; Mondrian bin pools all, so quantiles biased toward fast recoverers
minimum_data_needed: EDA/HRV time series during stress and meditation
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with slow EDA recovery (τ > median) will show meditation coverage <80%; fast recoverers will show coverage ≥88%
cards.failure_condition: EDA recovery time constant does not predict meditation coverage gap (p>0.05) after controlling for respiration variability
cards.statistical_test_plan: Per-subject nonlinear fit: EDA(t) = A*exp(-t/τ) + C during recovery; extract τ. Mixed model: meditation_coverage_gap ~ τ + respiration_rate_variability + (1|bin)
cards.falsification_test: Create separate Mondrian bins for slow vs fast recoverers (median split on τ); if undercoverage disappears for slow recoverers, mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified

cards.hypothesis: Feature extraction window alignment with stressor onset creates systematic nonconformity score bias for subjects with delayed physiological responses
cards.proposed_mechanism: WESAD uses fixed windows relative to condition onset; subjects with delayed EDA/HRV responses (latency > window) have features extracted from pre-response baseline, yielding artificially low nonconformity scores during calibration; test windows capture response, causing undercoverage
cards.causal_path: Subject trait (delayed physiological latency) → Fixed feature window misses response onset → Calibration features reflect baseline not stress → Nonconformity scores underestimated → Prediction sets calibrated to baseline variability → Test windows capture true response → Response exceeds prediction set → Undercoverage
control_variables: estimate per-subject latency and align windows
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to response magnitude variability, not latency
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage gap correlates with response magnitude, not with latency; latency-magnitude correlation is zero
cards.distinguishing_test: Estimate per-subject EDA latency (time from stressor to 10% peak); regress coverage gap on latency controlling for peak magnitude
cards.effect_size_rationale: EDA latency literature: 1-5s typical, but 10-20% subjects >10s; WESAD windows likely 10-30s; delayed responders may have 30-50% of response missed in calibration window
minimum_data_needed: High-resolution EDA/HRV time series aligned to stressor onset
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with EDA latency > feature_window_start will show undercoverage; coverage gap correlates with latency after controlling for magnitude
cards.failure_condition: EDA response latency does not predict coverage gap after controlling for peak magnitude (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Per-subject latency estimation via change-point detection on EDA phasic driver. Quantile regression: coverage_gap ~ latency + peak_magnitude
cards.falsification_test: Re-extract features using latency-aligned windows per subject; if undercoverage resolves for delayed responders, mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified

cards.hypothesis: Conformal prediction's marginal coverage guarantee interacts with WESAD's subject-level split to produce conditional undercoverage for subjects underrepresented in calibration
cards.proposed_mechanism: WESAD uses subject-wise split (some subjects only in test); Mondrian's conditional coverage guarantee holds only for categories with sufficient calibration representation; subjects with rare feature combinations have no calibration support, reverting to marginal coverage which undercovers their specific conditional distribution
cards.causal_path: Subject-wise train/test split → Rare feature combinations absent from calibration → Mondrian bins for test subjects empty or undersized → Conformal predictor falls back to marginal quantile → Marginal quantile narrower than true conditional quantile for rare subjects → Undercoverage
control_variables: minimum bin population threshold with merging
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to subject-specific distribution shift (covariate shift), not empty bins
cards.rival_prediction: Test subjects' feature vectors fall within calibration convex hull but coverage still low; empty-bin rate near zero
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute for each test subject: proportion of their test points falling in bins with calibration population <5. Correlate this proportion with coverage gap. Mechanism predicts strong correlation; rival predicts weak
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD has 15 subjects; typical split 10/5 or 12/3; with 5 conditions and Mondrian taxonomy, many bins empty for held-out subjects; marginal coverage 90% but conditional can be 50-70% for rare types
minimum_data_needed: Mondrian bin assignments for all points
cards.testable_prediction: Test subjects with >30% of points in empty/undersized bins will show coverage <75%; subjects with full bin support will show coverage ≥88%
cards.failure_condition: Proportion of points in undersized bins does not predict coverage gap (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Per-subject: undersized_bin_proportion = mean(bin_population_calibration < 5). Regression: coverage_gap ~ undersized_bin_proportion
cards.falsification_test: Use leave-one-subject-out cross-conformal (aggregate all other subjects as calibration for each test subject); if undercoverage disappears, mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified
